suites.name: chat-inbound-guard
suites.description: Chatbots: catch prompt injection and spam, and skip messages that need no reply.

suites.name: code-review-lint
suites.description: Engineering: flag swallowed errors, logged secrets and misleading commit messages.

suites.name: contract-risk
suites.description: Legal: flag auto-renewal, uncapped liability and one-sided change clauses.

suites.name: entity-match
suites.description: Data cleaning: decide whether two messy records are the same company, person or product.

suites.name: inbox-triage
suites.description: Personal: sort email into action, security, receipt, FYI, newsletter or spam.

suites.name: lead-routing
suites.description: Sales: route inbound leads to a sales call, self-serve, nurture or disqualify.

suites.name: model-routing
suites.description: LLM apps: decide whether a request needs a small, mid or frontier model.

suites.name: rag-fact-check
suites.description: AI apps: check whether a source supports, contradicts or never mentions a generated claim.

suites.name: review-moderation
suites.description: E-commerce: publish, hide or escalate product reviews under a store policy.

suites.name: support-triage
suites.description: Customer support: route emails to cancel, refund, billing, bug or how-to, and flag chargeback threats.

caveats: Each suite is 12–27 hand-labeled cases: a smoke test, not a benchmark. Differences of a point or two are noise.
The suites were written and tuned against Jev, so the comparison may lean in its favour.
Accuracy pools every labeled answer in a suite; mean accuracy weights each suite equally.
Automated at 95% is the share of cases above the lowest confidence cutoff where automated answers stay at least 95% correct.
Cost is what OpenRouter billed per call, averaged across suites. Jev called directly at TypeSafe costs the same list price.
A few models accept only plain-string state; they receive the same state serialized as JSON (marked †).
